evals.name: vague-idea-to-buildable-brief
evals.prompt: im building a thing for small law firms to manage their case files. i want it to feel professional and modern. can you help me figure out the design?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to accept professional and modern as direction. Asks who is looking and in what state before anything else. Generates two or three genuinely different framings, commits to one with a reason, and produces a brief whose surface list is specific enough to build from and whose negatives are named rather than implied.
assertions: Asked who the audience is and in what state they use it, before producing a brief
Did not accept professional and modern as design direction
Produced two or more genuinely different framings, not tonal variations on one
Recommended one framing with a reason rather than asking the user to choose between three
Named specific surfaces rather than writing the dashboard and the settings
Recorded named negatives - what it must never look like - rather than only positives
Recorded the runner-up framings and why they lost
Listed open questions with what each is waiting on

evals.name: resists-category-default
evals.prompt: we want to build an analytics product for ecommerce stores. show me what the design should be
evals.expected_output: Notices that the obvious framing - a metrics dashboard with cards and charts - is the category default that every competitor already has, and says so rather than inheriting it silently. At least one framing centres a different user or competes against a different alternative. Commits to one anyway, with reasoning.
assertions: Noticed and named that the obvious framing is the category default
Produced at least one framing that centres a different user or a different competing alternative
Did not silently inherit dashboard-of-cards as the product shape
Still committed to a single framing rather than leaving the choice open
Derived the focal hierarchy from a stated one thing it must do better

evals.name: thin-existing-brief
evals.prompt: we already wrote a design brief but the mockups keep coming back wrong. can you look at it? [brief contains: 'Audience: everyone. Style: clean, modern, professional, trustworthy. Surfaces: the app.']
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses why the brief produces wrong mockups - audience unnamed, surfaces unlisted, adjectives where decisions belong - rather than rewriting it cosmetically. Replaces each vague field with something that constrains downstream work, and asks the small number of questions it cannot answer from evidence.
assertions: Diagnosed specifically why the existing brief fails rather than just rewriting it
Identified that audience-as-everyone constrains nothing downstream
Identified that the surface list is not a work-list
Replaced adjectives with decisions that a later stage can act on
Asked only for what could not be derived from what already existed
Did not invent an audience to fill the gap
Derived the audience from the authority or the existing brief where those already stated it, rather than generating a new one

evals.name: fails-closed-without-codex
evals.prompt: help me work out the design brief for my new product
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight, finds codex unavailable, and stops. Names whether it is absent or signed out with the matching fix, and explains why divergent framings need the second model rather than treating the dependency as arbitrary.
assertions: Checked for codex before starting work
Refused to proceed rather than producing framings alone
Distinguished which of the three preflight states this was - not installed, unauthenticated, or installed but unreachable - and gave the fix matching that state
Explained why the collaboration is required for this stage specifically
Left no run folder implying the stage had completed

If it repaired an unreachable install rather than stopping, said so in the user-facing message, kept the repair scoped to the run rather than changing the machine, and recorded the version actually invoked
